platform_corner_junction_report.finding: The target and donor junction topologies differ, but replacing one cell splits the donor front row. The accepted patch keeps the coherent donor row, inherits the donors' exact ramp_south semantics, and trims canonical and donor cleanup carriers to their shared grid plane without importing source (18,-13) or lower dirt cell (18,-12).

observations: The alpha channel contains every value from 0 through 255; it is a continuous lawn/soil selector, not a binary opacity card.
At decoded x=256, y=260 the selector is clean soil alpha 0.
The recovered wavy transition band spans approximately decoded y=260 through y=336 and reaches source lawn alpha near 1 while retaining white RGB modulation.
FieldGroundShader01 inverts source UV2 V before sampling the lawn/soil mask.
The transition contour moves from decoded y=289 through y=315 across x, so the source boundary itself supplies the organic edge and must not be sine-warped by the editor.

Consecutive material-19 source dirt cells (19..21, -11) all use UV2 (-0.222876, -1.127860), while adjacent source lawn cells use (-0.101646, 0.928709); the repeat-equivalent lawn V=-1.071291 forms the nearest continuous atlas interval.

Those same dirt cells carry non-white Color0 values while the adjacent lawn cells carry white Color0, proving that an edited surface must inherit Color0 from the target surface family rather than the replaced cell.
The canonical ledge is a bowed multi-band profile, not a vertical quad scaled to an arbitrary height.
Source UV0 advances at one repeat per 300 cm; cliff UV1 and border UV2 advance by approximately 0.516 and 0.511 per source metre respectively.
Generated outside corners continue the same profile through a quarter arc so adjacent faces do not leave triangular holes.

decoded_ledge_fringe.observation: The recognizable leafy ledge silhouette is a separate FieldGrass material-13 sloped carrier. The opaque material-18 cliff shader can blend grass color into the face but cannot reproduce this cutout by itself.

implementation_contract.canonical_surface_reconstruction: Each generated top tile samples at a 21 by 21 lattice. The 5 cm spacing places the recovered 30 cm dirt-ribbon seam on exact row 6. The planar ribbon's organic silhouette comes from the source atlas rather than geometric tessellation; this density keeps the complete combined edited surface below the renderer's indexed-mesh submission ceiling. Material 19 alone donates the top-surface height and attributes; material 12/13 cliff and leafy-lip triangles cannot be selected accidentally. Authored cells retain canonical world-position UV0/UV1, rebuild UV2 from edited topology, and obtain Color0 from a deterministic world-space blend of the eight nearest canonical cells in the target surface and elevation family.
implementation_contract.lawn_uv_continuity: Every generated boundary vertex uses the canonical material-19 UV0/UV1 samples at the same source-space position. Target-surface Color0 is evaluated from world coordinates, so adjacent edited cells evaluate the identical value on their shared edge instead of switching donors at a tile boundary. This prevents replaced dirt tint from surviving as a rectangular dark lawn tile, prevents replaced lawn tint from making a dirt tile brighter than its path neighbors, and removes the west/east square delimiter around edited cell (19,-12).
implementation_contract.lawn_surface_selection: Light Lawn and Dark Lawn each expose one project prefab. Authored light lawn uses the recovered canonical lawn UV2 endpoint and target-family Color0; there are no independent per-cell lawn variants.
implementation_contract.geometric_seam_control: Canonical Route 1 ground planes sit 0.30 cm above their nominal 50 cm levels. Generated top surfaces therefore use level+0.32 cm: the source plane plus a 0.02 cm depth margin. Authored cells are merged into one continuous material-mode-4 render object. No neighboring cells create coplanar duplicate surfaces.
implementation_contract.authored_ground_scale: Authored flat cells and directional ramps use one world-continuous UV0/UV1 field at the measured 300 cm source repeat. The ramp slope changes height and normals without rotating or restarting the texture island.
implementation_contract.dirt_transition_sampling: Subdivided dirt-region edges are chained into contours before mesh generation. At a lawn seam, the outer 5 cm lattice row joins canonical clean-lawn UV2 V=0.928709 to boundary-lawn V=0.932880402; the remainder of the recovered 30 cm ribbon traverses to soil-side V=0.991155148. Paired U remains constant across the ribbon and advances along the contour at 0.36 repeats per metre. At the inner row, generated ribbon vertices retain that paired U instead of falling back to the unrelated clean-dirt U. The row is duplicated for clean-soil interior triangles, so no triangle interpolates across the repeat-distant UV seam. This reconstructs the source split topology, removes the false straight green inset, and prevents a boundary-atlas fragment from protruding at the outer lawn edge. Dirt tiles without exposed edges use the exact canonical clean-soil endpoint.
implementation_contract.dirt_path_prefab_family: The automatic Dirt Path prefab derives NESW links from all same-height neighboring dirt, whether source or authored. Sixteen explicit flat dirt prefabs additionally expose every path_0 through path_15 connection mask: north=1, east=2, south=4, and west=8. A set bit continues dirt through that side; an unset bit uses the recovered glassmask01_com grassy transition. This covers full dirt, four grass edges, four grass corners, two corridors, four dirt ends, and isolated dirt.
implementation_contract.automatic_connectivity: Automatic dirt remains the fast paint workflow. An untouched source dirt cell directly affected by an authored neighbor is regenerated in the same combined surface draw so the dirt side owns the newly required leafy edge; this dependency ring is not propagated through source lawn or farther across Route 1. Selecting an explicit dirt prefab replaces only that tile's derived mask with the persisted authored mask.
implementation_contract.legacy_compatibility: Previously saved lawn_a through lawn_d values remain accepted and normalize to auto. Existing path_0 through path_15 dirt values now retain their exact mask because they are first-class authoring choices.
implementation_contract.profiled_ledges: Every changed exposed height boundary builds the decoded four-band FieldCliffShader01 profile at each 50 cm tier, preserves the source UV roles, fills equal-height outside corners with a profiled quarter arc, and adds the decoded material-13 leafy fringe card at the top boundary. Shared sides retain the height of both endpoints, so a generated ramp-side boundary can taper to a matching corner instead of producing a misplaced full-width wall. Boundaries owned by an untouched source tile but exposed by an authored neighbor are included in the dependency ring rather than being skipped.
implementation_contract.canonical_source_reference_tiles: Authored-scene schema 4 adds an optional terrain source_reference coordinate. The Route runtime groups adjacent references by their exact grid translation, unions the donor cells, and clips that connected patch from the immutable canonical geometry. Each target inherits its donor's exact elevation, surface, and flat/ramp profile before boundary classification, so logical topology cannot drift from the rendered donor mesh. This retains donor ground, cliff, leafy-fringe, and cleanup render objects with their original material and source vertex streams while preventing a triangle crossing an internal donor-cell boundary from being cloned twice. Generated tops and ledges are suppressed on referenced cells and shared edges. A height-changing outer edge retains required donor spill plus cleanup triangles wholly inside the adjacent cell's decoded 25 cm cliff band. At a same-profile edge, centroid ownership is resolved first and retained canonical/donor cleanup vertices are trimmed to the common source-grid plane, preventing overlap without extending donor ownership into a neighboring source cell. Route 1 maps canonical (19..21,-13..-15) to target (14..16,-13..-15) as one coherent patch; its west boundary clips donor source x=1900 cm to translated target x=1400 cm. The Inspector exposes each donor and the tile clipboard preserves it; any ordinary surface/profile edit deliberately leaves source-reference mode.
implementation_contract.dirt_ramp_highlight: Editable dirt ramps remain on material mode 4 and transfer the exact low-edge, low-center, and high Color0 controls measured on the material-19 ground ramp beside the sign. Their sub-one alpha activates FieldGroundShader01's authored Alpha_light term. Matching-height flat dirt neighbors blend from the shared high- or low-side ramp control back to their normal target-family Color0 across one tile. Every matching-profile dirt/lawn boundary, whether the dirt is flat or a ramp, receives the neighboring lawn's continuous target-family Color0 at the shared seam and blends back to its dirt field over the recovered 30 cm ribbon. This fixes both the north flat-dirt and south ramp-dirt sides of cell (19,-12) without recoloring either surface interior. The rejected material-18 cliff-rim interpretation and mode 27 remain removed.
implementation_contract.tile_19_four_edge_regression: Cell (19,-12) is authored light lawn between light-lawn cells (18,-12)/(20,-12), flat dirt (19,-11), and ramp-south dirt (19,-13). West and east must share the same world-space Color0 field; north and south must meet the lawn endpoint exactly and resolve through the recovered 30 cm ground ribbon. No side may select an independent per-cell donor or expose a straight tint delimiter.
implementation_contract.local_fragment_cleanup: Masking is material-aware: material-19 terrain assembly groups are conservative source ground, while material-12/13/18 ledge and foliage groups are cleanup layers when source geometry changes. Ordinary replacements remove crossing cleanup triangles on any vertex touch. They now also compare the edited and canonical endpoint profiles on every exposed neighbor edge: if the edit invalidates the source ledge, the complete decoded 25 cm companion band is removed from the neighbor side even when all three vertices remain a few centimetres outside the edited cell. At board junction (20,-13)/(20,-12), this retires canonical mesh-34 material-18 triangle 192 and its assembly copy; leaving it produced the tapered brown wedge reported beside (21,-12). Exact source-reference cells retain separate centroid/donor ownership. At transplanted target (15,-12)/(15,-13), that same source triangle 192 remains required because it completes triangle 191 and cliff triangles 448-451 in the deliberately retained donor band. Matching-profile boundaries do not trigger the new removal. Cleanup beyond 25.5 cm is neither removed nor imported, and no triangle is collapsed onto z=-1200 cm. Large canonical ground groups retain centroid masking.
implementation_contract.editor_platform_tools: The terrain palette separates Ground, Ramps, and Platforms into explicit modes. The Scene toolbar and Inspector independently toggle exact source-grid (X,Z) coordinates and saved elevation profiles; flat cells display L# while directional profiles display L#-L#+1. Hover always reports coordinate, saved profile, and surface, and selected footprints expose a copyable coordinate reference. The cyan ghost projects every prospective corner rather than flattening the preview. Tile Profile defaults to preserving each selected cell's current flat/ramp shape and also offers per-cell Restore Source Profile, Force Flat, and four explicit directions. Build / Replace Profiled Platform applies one low/base level, surface, selected profile policy, and automatic visual variant as one undoable edit. Connected cells suppress internal walls; compatible canonical leafy fringe stays intact, while changed exposed boundaries rebuild the material-13 leafy carrier, material-18 bowed cliff, and outside corners. The three source-style +1 platform cards remain quick presets.
implementation_contract.editor_tile_clipboard: Copy Selected / Ctrl+C sorts the selected sparse footprint and uses its first real tile as both the positional and height anchor. Every stamp cell stores signed X/Z offsets, signed elevation from that anchor, its original absolute Route elevation, surface, flat/ramp shape, visual variant, and optional canonical source reference. Paste Exact Height / Ctrl+V restores absolute elevations and donor references for source-platform repair. Paste Relative to Anchor / Ctrl+Shift+V maps the copied anchor to one destination cell while preserving all signed tier offsets. Both validate every destination and donor before persistence and apply the complete stamp as one autosaved undoable edit; neighbor-derived dirt transitions, ramp lighting, and ledge geometry then rebuild.
implementation_contract.board_side_platform_repair: The final repair does not flatten or approximate the retained platform end. Nine target cells (14..16,-13..-15) reference source (19..21,-13..-15) with one (-5,0) translation, preserving a coherent front row and both rear rows. The three front-row targets inherit the donors' exact elevation-2 dark_lawn ramp_south profiles. At the matching west edge, donor cleanup carriers are trimmed to source x=1900 cm and canonical target cleanup carriers are trimmed to target x=1400 cm after centroid ownership. Source (18,-13) is not transplanted, so target (13,-13) keeps its canonical ground, logical connection into (13,-12), and correctly oriented west side beside (12,-13). The north edge from (14,-13) to (14,-12) changes height, so the exact donor cliff and leafy fringe remain. Board cells, board registration, and all other user-authored terrain remain unchanged.
implementation_contract.persistence: Light Lawn, Dark Lawn, Empty, ramps, and the automatic Dirt Path emit visual_variant=auto. Explicit flat dirt-path prefabs emit and retain visual_variant=path_0 through path_15 in the generic authored-scene document. Manual connection masks are intentionally rejected for ramp shapes.

claim_boundary: LGPE stores continuous route-authored ground paint rather than a reusable 1 m tile atlas. The modular tile topology is an editor/runtime reconstruction that reuses the exact recovered material, UV semantics, and source transition signal; it is not claimed to be an original Game Freak tile index table.
